html:
Efraín Ríos Montt was a Guatemalan general who ruled Guatemala after a coup from March 1982 to August 1983, the bloodiest period of the civil war. In 2013 he was convicted of genocide.

An evangelical Protestant preacher, he gave Sunday sermons on television. His army's campaign against the guerrillas in the highlands, called "beans and bullets", destroyed Maya villages, killing thousands of men, women and children, especially among the Ixil Maya. He was removed by another coup.

He later returned to politics and led Congress. In 2013 a court in Guatemala City found him guilty of genocide against the Ixil, the first such verdict against a former head of state by a national court. The verdict was overturned on procedural grounds days later, and he died during a retrial. His trial was a landmark for the victims of the civil war in Guatemala.
sum: Efraín Ríos Montt was a Guatemalan general who ruled Guatemala after a coup from March 1982 to August 1983, the bloodiest period of the civil war. In 2013 he was convicted of genocide.
